onboarding.title: Welcome to GuideTrain
onboarding.subtitle: A few quick details so we can tailor your training.
onboarding.bodyWeightWhy: Used as the load for push-ups, chin-ups and the other bodyweight exercises.

explorer.hint: Rotate the model, filter by region, and tap a muscle.

viewer.pairWhy: Different regions, so neither tires the other.

addExercise.duplicate: That's very close to "{name}" — already on the list.

abs.name: Rectus Abdominis
abs.desc: The 'six-pack'; flexes the spine, resists extension. Crunches, leg raises, planks.

add.name: Adductors
add.desc: Inner thigh; pulls the legs together, stabilises hips. Adduction, sumo squats.

bic.name: Biceps Brachii
bic.desc: Front of the upper arm; bends the elbow, supinates the forearm. Curls.

calf.name: Gastrocnemius / Calf
calf.desc: Two-headed calf bulge; points the toes (plantarflexion). Standing calf raises.

delt.name: Deltoid
delt.desc: Shoulder cap in three heads; raises the arm every direction. Presses, lateral raises.

erector.name: Erector Spinae
erector.desc: Columns beside the spine; extends and stabilises the back. Deadlifts, back extensions.

fore.name: Forearm
fore.desc: Grip, wrist and finger drivers. Wrist curls, grip work, carries.

glute.name: Gluteus Maximus
glute.desc: Largest muscle; extends the hip, drives power. Squats, hip thrusts, bridges.

ham.name: Hamstrings
ham.desc: Back-thigh group; bends the knee, extends the hip. RDLs, leg curls, deadlifts.

lat.name: Latissimus Dorsi
lat.desc: The 'wings' of the back; pulls the arms down and back. Pull-ups, rows, pulldowns.

neck.name: Neck
neck.desc: Sternocleidomastoid and neck extensors; turns and steadies the head. Neck curls, shrugs, harness work.

obl.name: External Oblique
obl.desc: Flanks of the abdomen; rotates and side-bends the trunk. Twists, side planks.

pec.name: Pectoralis Major
pec.desc: Chest fan; pushes and draws the arm across the body. Bench press, flyes, push-ups.

quad.name: Quadriceps
quad.desc: Front-thigh group of four; straightens the knee. Squats, lunges, leg extensions.

shin.name: Tibialis Anterior
shin.desc: Front of the shin; lifts the foot (dorsiflexion). Toe raises, walks.

traps.name: Trapezius
traps.desc: Upper back & neck yoke; shrugs and stabilises the shoulder blades. Shrugs, face-pulls.

tri.name: Triceps Brachii
tri.desc: Back of the upper arm; straightens the elbow. Dips, pushdowns, overhead extensions.

workout.title: Workout
workout.empty: Nothing saved yet. Open a muscle and press + beside an exercise to build a workout.
workout.finishedLast: That is the last workout in this plan done. Start the plan again when you are ready.

swap.title: Swap {name}
swap.intro: Exercises that train the same muscle — pick one to replace it with.
swap.empty: No swap found for this exercise.

calisthenics.title: Calisthenics
calisthenics.intro: Every bodyweight exercise in one place — tap + to add one to your workout, tap a name for instructions.
calisthenics.empty: Nothing here for this muscle yet.

stretching.title: Stretching
stretching.intro: Browse only — nothing here is logged. Tap a name for instructions, tap Hold for a timer.
stretching.empty: Nothing here for this muscle yet.

plan.title: Getting stronger
plan.trainingMax: Working from a training max of {tm} {unit} — {percent}% of the estimate, on purpose.

answer.one: {count} cycle, about {weeks} weeks, adding {increment} {unit} each time.
answer.other: {count} cycles, about {weeks} weeks, adding {increment} {unit} each time.

plan.already: You are already there. Set a higher target.
plan.needSet: Log a set of {count} reps or fewer for this exercise and a plan appears here.
plan.amrapNote: + means take the last set for as many good reps as you can, not to failure.
plan.barbellNote: 5/3/1 was written for the main barbell lifts. The percentages still work here, but the jumps assume something you can load heavily.
plan.estimateNote: An estimate from one set, not a measurement. If a week feels wrong, it is the plan that is wrong.
plan.repeatNote: The same four weeks repeat each cycle, with {increment} {unit} added to the training max — that is where the increase comes from.
plan.lightNote: The weekly jumps are small on purpose. Every load is a share of the training max, not of your real one, so a cycle never asks for a maximum lift; the work comes from the + sets.
plan.sameLoads: Same weights as the cycle before. {increment} {unit} on the training max is less than the smallest jump a bar can make with {plate} {unit} plates, so it rounds away here and shows up in the next cycle.
plan.useWeekNote: Take a week and its weights go into your workout, offered back one set at a time as you log.
plan.stalled: You missed {week}: {reps} reps at {load} {unit}, and it asks for {required}.
plan.stallWhy: That is the training max telling you it is too high. The fix is not to try again heavier — back it off {percent}% and rebuild. Two steps forward, one step back is what keeps this running for years.
plan.tmReset: Training max set by hand: {tm} {unit}, down from the {from} {unit} your lifts imply.
plan.hitTitle: {reps} reps — the {required} it asks for, or better.
plan.missedTitle: {reps} reps, short of the {required} it asks for.
plan.ambiguous: Two weeks of this cycle call for the same top weight, so a logged set cannot be told apart between them. Neither is marked.

step.model: Drag to rotate. Tap any muscle to see what trains it.
step.add: Tap + to send it to today's workout — we've added {name} here to show you.
step.workout: Everything you've added lives here, in the order you'll do it.
step.log: Enter what you lifted, then tap Add set. That's the whole loop.
step.plans: Or skip the building — apply a full program in one tap.
step.help: That's the tour. Tap this any time you want to see it again.

target.editClears: Your own sets and reps replace the weights above.
target.refreshNote: Stays at this weight until you tap Refresh, even if your maxes change.
target.refreshSame: Already up to date — no change.
target.refreshNoData: Not enough data yet to recalculate this.

plans.title: Ready-made plans
plans.intro: Pick a shape, see the weights you would actually use, and it becomes your workouts.
plans.startingNote: Weights marked “starting point” come from your body weight and age — a population average, not a measurement of you. Treat the first set as a test: if it moves easily, add weight; if it does not, take some off. Once you log a set, that lift uses your own numbers instead.
plans.knownMaxNote: Weights marked “your set max” come from the max you set on the Stats page for this lift, not a logged set — a real number, just not measured here yet. Log a set and it takes over.
plans.relatedNote: Weights marked “from” another lift are scaled from a known max on that lift, not measured on this one — a real number, just not this bar's. Set your own on the Stats page.
plans.cycleNote: Squat, bench, deadlift and overhead press each carry their own training max here — the same one Plan → uses for that lift everywhere else in the app. A lift with nothing logged and no training max set shows “pick your own” for its first week; open Plan → on it after adding the workout to set one.
plans.percentNote: Each session asks for a set percent of your best known max on this lift, applied directly rather than estimated from the reps — the program's own numbers, not this app's usual working-weight guess.
plans.loggedNote: Sets are meant to be finished, not to end you — roughly one or two reps left in the tank.

fullbody.name: Full body
fullbody.desc: Two alternating sessions covering everything, on the big barbell lifts. The usual place to start.

upperlower.name: Upper / lower
upperlower.desc: Splits the body in two so each half is trained twice a week. A step up in volume.

ppl.name: Push / pull / legs
ppl.desc: Groups by movement rather than body part. More exercises per session, fewer muscles.

plans.carryNote: These weights go into your workout, offered back one set at a time as you log.

bodypart.name: Body part split
bodypart.desc: One muscle group a day, four or five days a week — more volume per session, low weekly frequency. The classic bodybuilding split, sized to how many days you actually have.

dumbbell.name: Dumbbell-only full body
dumbbell.desc: The same full-body shape, built entirely from dumbbells — no barbell or rack required. For a home gym, or a commercial one when the rack is always busy.

minimal.name: Minimal, two days a week
minimal.desc: Four lifts, twice a week — a squat, a deadlift, a press and a pull, nothing extra. For when two sessions is what you actually have.

noequip.name: Bodyweight only
noequip.desc: No added weight — push-ups, pull-ups and bodyweight squats, using nothing but a bar to hang from. For travel, a hotel room, or starting out with nothing.

stronglifts.name: StrongLifts 5×5
stronglifts.desc: Three sessions a week, alternating two workouts, five sets of five on the big lifts. The same shape as Full body, run heavier and faster.

gzclp.name: GZCLP
gzclp.desc: Four days, three tiers — one heavy lift, one lighter, one light accessory. A structured way to keep progressing once a straight-set plan stops moving.

531.desc: Four main lifts, each on its own weekly cycle off a training max that only ever climbs in small steps, with assistance work alongside. The same system as Plan →, for all four lifts at once.

sixday.name: 6-day split
sixday.desc: Chest & back, shoulders & arms, and legs, each trained twice a week — a different exercise selection the second time round rather than the same session repeated. High volume, six sessions a week.

russian.name: Russian Squat, Bench & Deadlift
russian.desc: The Russian Squat Routine's shape, run on all three lifts in turn — squat, then bench, then deadlift, three sessions a week off a percent of your max, the same weight and reps within a week then heavier and shorter the next. Eighteen weeks total, six brutally repetitive weeks per lift, one of the most-cited ways to add 5–10% to a lift fast. One lift at a time on purpose, not all three together: this frequency is already a lot for a single lift, and deadlift especially isn't usually trained this often.

load.barOnly: Just the bar — nothing on it.
load.perHandNote: One dumbbell's weight — not the pair combined.
load.barTotalNote: The bar's total weight — plates included.

history.title: History
history.empty: Nothing logged yet. Sets you record appear here.

account.title: Account
account.confirmSent: Check your email to confirm the account, then sign in.
account.why: Signing in keeps your training on this device and syncs it to your account, so a lost phone does not lose it.
account.signOutNote: Your training stays on this device. Signing out only stops it from also going to your account.
account.merging: Bringing this device and your account together…
account.resetSent: Check your email for a link to reset your password.
account.recoveryIntro: Set a new password to finish signing in.
account.recoveryDone: Password changed — close this panel to continue.
account.emailChangeSent: Check your new address for a link to confirm the change.
account.deleteLocalData: Delete all data on this device
account.deleteLocalDataWarning: This clears every set, workout and stat saved on this device — nothing is backed up anywhere. This cannot be undone.
account.deleteLocalDataWarningSynced: This clears every set, workout and stat saved on this device. Your account keeps its own copy — sign in again to bring it back.
account.deleteLocalDataConfirm: Yes, delete everything on this device
account.deleteAccountWarning: This permanently deletes your account and everything in it — every set, workout and stat, on every device. This cannot be undone.

equipmentPanel.title: Equipment
equipmentPanel.intro: What you actually have access to right now, not a permanent fact about you — pick as many as apply. Exercise lists reorder to put these first; nothing is hidden.
equipmentPanel.bodyweightNote: Bodyweight exercises — push-ups, pull-ups and the rest — always count as available, since they need nothing to try.

injuryPanel.title: Injuries
injuryPanel.intro: Mark a muscle you're working around, and choose how the app should respond. "Avoid" keeps anything that trains it out of Train This, rest-break partners and swaps. "Warn" leaves every one of those lists exactly as it was, only flagged.
injuryPanel.note: This only changes what gets suggested or flagged from here on — nothing already in a saved workout is removed for you.

stats.title: Progress
stats.overrideFrom: Set by hand, over the {from} {unit} your log implies.
stats.overrideNoLog: Set by hand — nothing logged for this lift yet.

goals.title: Goals
goals.limit: Up to {max} goals at once — remove one to add another.
goals.noBasis: Log a set for this lift, or set a max, to see your pace.

export.title: Export for AI feedback
export.intro: Your profile, current program, maxes, goals and full training log, as one file — paste it into any AI chat for feedback on progress, planning or what to try next.
